title: Simultaneous Coverage of Sensitivity Regions for Fixed-Effects Counterfactual Forecasts under One-Time Adoption
banked_reason: D-0.5 proposal search exhausted all three seeds at the fixed field floor; reviewed candidates were sound only at letter tier, and the final consulted operator/inference repair returned needs-pivot.
gap_reasons: tier=letter below novelty_target=field: the stated field-level consequence rests on an unimplemented population-mean decision and lacks a verified comparison showing that the proposed narrow calibration envelope advances whole-region support inference beyond the closest literature.
The advertised sensitivity decision uses an assumed population reported mean mu, while the sampling model supplies no estimator or joint inference for mu and the calibration envelope.

FE(P,q) is not determined by P and q: the fit permits iota to depend on the full Yobs, including unrestricted treated post outcomes, while those treatment effects and their relation to mu are unspecified; hence the asserted untreated-moment projection and ensuing decision target do not follow from the defined experiment.
proof_attempt_summary: Three distinct proposal roots were pursued under the fixed field novelty floor: a pinned attainable-design benchmark, a pooled staggered calibration diagnostic, and a learned support-envelope/inference program. The reviewed candidates remained letter-tier; the final route also required a training-only FEct operator, joint effect estimation, and a strict valid comparator gain, and the bounded author declined that repair as not authorable. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization began; a future re-raise would need a genuinely new field-level root.
tldr: For a family of one-adoption panel forecasts, can a learned sharp FEct calibration region receive honest simultaneous support coverage at exposed faces and change a first-horizon sensitivity decision relative to a coarse primitive band? The proposed method combines a directly specified population FEct training operator, fractional-rank tail moments, and a near-optimal multiplier envelope. The seven-date mixture is a diagnostic member of a broader design family, not the whole contribution.
gap: Existing FEct sensitivity procedures use chosen bias restrictions for scalar targets; support-process and directional-bootstrap results do not automatically handle a continuum-threshold, full-tail FEct region with direction switches.
fill: Establish the FEct projection and sharp region for the family, prove locally uniform whole-region outer coverage, derive the local switch process, and prove or refute strict critical-value and decision gain on an open subfamily.
